degreeMatrix.caption: Explore how the five functional degrees operate within a single scale (C–D–E–F–G–A–B♭–C). Select any role to highlight its position and hear a short phrase demonstrating its function.

roles.name: Shāhed (ش)
roles.description: Shāhed (G): The melodic center of gravity. Notice how the phrase repeatedly returns to and dwells on G, bearing witness to the mode.

roles.name: Khātemeh (خ)
roles.description: Khātemeh (D): Definitive final closure. The descending cadence settles firmly on D, signaling that the piece has concluded.

roles.name: Īst (ی)
roles.description: Īst (F): Temporary pause. The phrase halts on F, creating a suspended breath that makes the listener anticipate continuation.

roles.name: Moteghayyer (م)
roles.description: Moteghayyer (B♮ / B♭): Variable degree. Pulled up to B♮ (493.88 Hz) when ascending to C5, then relaxed to B♭ (466.16 Hz) when descending.

roles.name: Āghāz (آ)
roles.description: Āghāz (E): Initial pitch. Launches the opening contour toward the Shāhed (G), though changing the starting note does not alter the maqām.

shahedComparison.caption: Compare a single-Shāhed melodic center (as in Darāmad II of Navā) with a dual-Shāhed balance (as in Darāmad I of Rāst-Panjgāh).

modes.title: Single Shāhed (e.g., Darāmad II of Navā)
modes.description: Melodic gravity orbits a single focal pitch (G, marked ش), giving the phrase a unified, concentrated axis.

modes.title: Dual Shāhed (e.g., Darāmad I of Rāst-Panjgāh)
modes.description: Melodic emphasis alternates between two focal degrees (F and A, both marked ش), creating a balanced two-pole modal tension.

moteghayyerLab.caption: Hear directional pitch attraction on a Moteghayyer (م) degree: raised when ascending toward the upper neighbor, lowered when descending toward the lower neighbor.

variants.label: Ascending Pull (Raised م → B♮)
variants.description: Moving upward toward C5, the Moteghayyer is pulled higher to B♮ (493.88 Hz) to narrow the step into C5.

variants.label: Descending Pull (Lowered م → B♭)
variants.description: Moving downward away from C5, the Moteghayyer relaxes to B♭ (466.16 Hz) to lean closer toward A and G.

variants.label: Full Arch (B♮ Up → B♭ Down)
variants.description: Combined melodic arch: the exact same scale degree (7th) shifts from B♮ in ascent to B♭ in descent.
